tasks.title: Free playground
tasks.instructions: Write any Python you like and press Run. It's a scratchpad for trying out ideas from your lessons.
requirements: Experiment freely - nothing here is graded or saved
tasks.hint: Try changing a value and running the program again to see how the output changes.
tasks.starterCode: # Write any Python code here and press Run

tasks.title: Your first program
tasks.instructions: Write a program that introduces you using print().
requirements: Print a line saying hello
Print one fact about yourself
Print the result of adding two numbers
Add a comment explaining your code
tasks.example:
Hello!
I am learning Python
12
tasks.hint: Each print() puts its text on a new line. Numbers don't need quotes: print(7 + 5).
tasks.starterCode:
# Your first program
# Use print() to show three lines

tasks.title: Shopping bill
tasks.instructions: Store the number of pens and notebooks you bought in variables, then work out and print the total number of items.
requirements: Create a variable for pens and one for notebooks
Create a variable total that adds them
Print total
tasks.hint: total = pens + notebooks

tasks.title: Type detective
tasks.instructions: A friend's age was saved as text: age_text = "14". Print its type, convert it to a whole number, then print the age they will be in 5 years.
requirements: Print type(age_text)
Convert it with int() into a new variable
Print the age in 5 years
tasks.example:
<class 'str'>
19
tasks.hint: "14" + 5 is an error, but int("14") + 5 works.

tests.expectedOutput:
<class 'str'>
19
tests.description: Prints the type, then the age in 5 years

tasks.title: Greeting program
tasks.instructions: Write a Python program that asks the user for their name and prints a greeting.
requirements: Ask for the user's name with input()
Print a greeting that includes the name
tasks.example:
Enter your name: Arnav
Hello Arnav
tasks.hint: name = input("Enter your name: ") stores whatever the user types.

tests.expectedOutput:
Enter your name: Arnav
Hello Arnav
tests.description: Your greeting includes the name Arnav

tests.expectedOutput:
Enter your name: Meera
Hello Meera
tests.description: Your greeting includes the name Meera

tests.expectedOutput:
Enter your name: Zoya Khan
Hello Zoya Khan

tasks.title: Birthday maths
tasks.instructions: Ask the user for their name and age, then tell them how old they will be next year using an f-string.
requirements: Read the name with input()
Read the age and convert it with int()
Print a sentence with an f-string
tasks.example:
Name: Meera
Age: 15
Meera, next year you will be 16
tasks.hint: input() always gives text - wrap it in int() before adding 1.

tests.expectedOutput:

Age: 15
Meera, next year you will be 16

Name: Ravi
Age: 41
Ravi, next year you will be 42

Name: Asha
Age: 99
Asha, next year you will be 100

tasks.title: Number comparer
tasks.instructions: Ask the user for two whole numbers and print the result of comparing them.
requirements: Read two numbers with int(input(...))
Print whether the first is greater than the second
Print whether they are equal
tasks.example:
First: 8
Second: 3
8 > 3 is True
8 == 3 is False
tasks.hint: print(a > b) prints True or False.

tests.expectedOutput:
First: 8
Second: 3
8 > 3 is True
8 == 3 is False

First: 4
Second: 4
4 > 4 is False
4 == 4 is True

First: 2
Second: 5
2 > 5 is False
2 == 5 is False

tasks.title: Can I vote?
tasks.instructions: Ask for the user's age. If they are 18 or older print that they can vote, otherwise print how many years they have to wait.
requirements: Convert the age to a number
Use if and else
Calculate the years left in the else branch
tasks.example:
Age: 15
You can vote in 3 years

You can vote in 3 years

Check the highest grade first

tasks.title: Cafe order

Ask with exactly: Item: and then Size (leave empty for medium):
If the size is empty (""), call order_text(item) so the default is used

Print the sentence it returns

requirements: Create a list with the seven names Monday to Sunday, in order

Print exactly: Day <number> is <name>

tasks.title: Marks analyser
tasks.instructions: Store five marks in a list, add one more with append(), then print the highest, the lowest and the average mark.
requirements: Create a list of marks

Print max, min and the average

Average: 72.5

tasks.title: Sale prices
tasks.instructions: A shop takes the same amount off every price during a sale. Use list comprehensions to make the sale prices, and a list of the sale prices that are under 50.
requirements: Keep prices = [120, 80, 45, 300] from the starter code
Ask with exactly: Discount: (a whole number)
Make sale with a list comprehension: every price minus the discount
Make cheap with a list comprehension: the sale prices under 50
Print exactly: Sale prices: <sale> and then Under 50: <cheap>
tasks.example:
Discount: 10
Sale prices: [110, 70, 35, 290]
Under 50: [35]

tasks.title: Bank account
tasks.instructions: Model a simple bank account with a class. The user names the owner, then deposits and withdraws until they quit. The account must never go below zero.
requirements: Define class Account with __init__(self, owner, balance=0) and the methods deposit(self, amount) and withdraw(self, amount)
withdraw prints exactly Not enough money (and changes nothing) when amount is more than the balance
Ask with exactly: Owner: then repeatedly Action (deposit/withdraw/quit):
For deposit or withdraw ask with exactly: Amount: , call the method, then print exactly: Balance: <balance>
For any other action except quit print exactly: Unknown action (and do not ask for an amount)
After quit print exactly: <owner> finished with Rs <balance>
tasks.example:
Owner: Asha
Action (deposit/withdraw/quit): deposit
Amount: 500
Balance: 500
Action (deposit/withdraw/quit): quit
Asha finished with Rs 500
tasks.hint: Make one object with acc = Account(owner). Inside the loop use if action == "quit": break, then elif branches for deposit and withdraw, and else for Unknown action.

tasks.title: Book shelf
tasks.instructions: Catalogue the books on a shelf. Each book is an object that knows how to print itself. After reading all the books, print them and name the longest one.
requirements: Define class Book with __init__(self, title, author, pages) and __str__ that returns exactly: <title> by <author>, <pages> pages
Ask with exactly: How many books? then for each book Title: , Author: and Pages: (pages is a whole number)
Keep the Book objects in a list
If there are no books print exactly: No books
Otherwise print every book with print(book), in the order they were typed, then print exactly: Longest: <title>. If books tie, the first one wins
tasks.example:
How many books? 1
Title: Malgudi Days
Author: R. K. Narayan
Pages: 256
Malgudi Days by R. K. Narayan, 256 pages
Longest: Malgudi Days
tasks.hint: __str__ must return the text, not print it. Start with longest = books[0] and only replace it when book.pages > longest.pages.
